sonnet.reason: The marker assertions can't catch the enumeration race, but the --git-dir/--work-tree argv assertions do fail when status is moved back onto the clone (B reproduced this), so the gap is only weak test coverage with no runtime effect.

terra.reason: The marker assertions do not exercise a filter added between key enumeration and use, although the separate repository-path assertions catch the reproduced isolation regression.

sonnet.reason: A paused rebase with a clean tree is accepted and its intermediate commit is pushed and landed (B reproduced this, and the base behaves the same), but an operator has to run the land script mid-rebase, and the commit that lands is the one that was checked.

terra.reason: A clean worktree paused partway through a rebase can cause the script to land an intermediate commit that omits later PR work.

sonnet.reason: The operator cannot remove the redundant runtime row and the warning repeats, but startup works and the retained entry is documented for rollback compatibility, so the effect is only a persistent diagnostic.

terra.reason: A redundant stored row cannot be removed through the catalog command, so its startup warning continues even though the built-in remains active.

sonnet.reason: Only a future built-in colliding with an existing runtime row would fail startup, and this change adds no such collision, so it is speculative.

terra.reason: A future built-in that collides with an existing runtime entry could prevent startup, although that collision policy already existed before this change.

sonnet.reason: The test hard-codes the decision date and eval ids, so it must be edited at the next decision, but runtime behavior is unaffected.

terra.reason: A later owner decision may require updating the hard-coded test expectations, with no demonstrated runtime effect.

sonnet.reason: The snapshot filter hides Haiku 5.5 in widened chains for every role and weakens regression coverage, with no runtime effect.

terra.reason: Filtering Haiku 5.5 from the frozen snapshot leaves its widened routing behavior outside that test, although widening itself follows the existing routing rules.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that the daemon refuses to start after upgrade when a stored operator routing cell uses an effort the built-in Haiku 5.5 lacks, which requires a runtime row with extra efforts plus a saved routing cell using one.

terra.reason: A persisted operator route using an effort supported by the old runtime definition but not the new built-in causes the daemon to fail at startup.

sonnet.reason: The pin reason text drops earlier rationale that is still preserved in EVIDENCE.md, so this is a documentation wording matter only.

terra.reason: The displayed pin reason omits earlier rationale, which remains available in the referenced evidence document.

sonnet.reason: Rerunning setup against a healthy daemon writes config but the daemon keeps using old settings until restarted, and setup reports success.

terra.reason: Rerunning setup against a healthy daemon reports success while the daemon continues using stale configuration.

sonnet.reason: Smoke verification uses fixed built-in providers rather than the configured catalog, so newly configured providers are never live-checked while setup reports success.

terra.reason: The new setup verification checks static providers and endpoints instead of the effective configured providers.

sonnet.reason: Init persists a repository without checking access and reports success, so SSO or permission problems surface only later; this needs an inaccessible repo.

terra.reason: A newly selected inaccessible repository is saved without the repository access check detecting the problem.

sonnet.reason: The discreet-mode question is not offered, but the feature does not exist yet (#37), so nothing functional is lost.

terra.reason: Interactive setup omits the requested discreet-mode choice and does not save the preference.

sonnet.reason: Doctor only checks that the OpenRouter key variable exists and never probes the provider, so a bad key or dead endpoint passes; this applies only when OpenRouter is configured.

terra.reason: Doctor accepts the presence of an OpenRouter key without checking whether the configured provider or credential works.

sonnet.reason: The native provider stays in the catalog regardless, so skipping the explicit entry only omits an entry and a summary line.

terra.reason: A preset alias suppresses an explicit native provider entry and its summary, but the native provider and models remain available.

sonnet.reason: A user with only one CLI passes doctor with a warning, but setup then runs smoke checks for the missing CLI and fails.

terra.reason: Setup accepts a missing Codex CLI during preflight but subsequently schedules smoke checks that require it.

sonnet.reason: Signal commands inside double-quoted command substitutions or unquoted heredocs evade the advisory warning detector, but an agent reaching for kill would normally use the plain forms that are detected.

terra.reason: Executable signal commands hidden in quoted substitutions or unquoted heredocs bypass the new warning check, though these forms are uncommon for sending signals.

sonnet.reason: A process.kill inside a template-literal ${...} interpolation is stripped along with the literal and goes undetected, which needs a contrived construction.

terra.reason: A signal call inside a JavaScript template interpolation bypasses the new warning check, but that form is a contrived way to send a signal.

sonnet.reason: The standard --eval=CODE form of node's inline eval is missed while the space-separated form is flagged, a realistic alternative syntax that silently skips the warning.

terra.reason: The standard --eval=CODE syntax bypasses the new warning check and is a realistic alternative to the separately quoted form.

sonnet.reason: Every tool-enabled Codex run is wrapped in a write-restricted sandbox while CODEX_HOME still points at the unwritable user state directory, so Codex fails to initialize in default configuration (reproduced with a read-only CODEX_HOME).

terra.reason: The new sandbox denies writes to the usual Codex state directory, preventing normal tool-enabled Codex agents from initializing.

sonnet.reason: Ordinary PDFs, MP4s and other requested inert media extensions are falsely blocked by the audit without 'Allow: binary', a reproduced false block on common files.

terra.reason: Ordinary files in explicitly requested media formats are incorrectly blocked unless a binary allowance is granted.

sonnet.reason: Valid PNGs with common tEXt/iTXt/iCCP metadata chunks fail the parser and lose the exemption, reproduced with a CRC-valid tEXt chunk.

terra.reason: Valid PNGs with common text or color-profile metadata are incorrectly blocked as opaque binaries.

sonnet.reason: A media file is falsely blocked only if its sample or pixel data happens to contain a signature like 'MZ', which needs specific byte content and is rare in practice.

terra.reason: Incidental byte patterns in valid media are mistaken for executable payloads and cause false audit blocks.

sonnet.reason: A large-resolution PNG that decodes to more than 32 MiB (for example 4096x4096) is falsely blocked, an uncommon but realistic input.

terra.reason: A valid high-resolution PNG can exceed the decoded-size cap and be incorrectly blocked despite its small file size.

sonnet.reason: Media files over 32 MiB, such as large WAVs or videos, are falsely blocked by the input size cap, which is uncommon but realistic.

terra.reason: A valid media file larger than 32 MiB is incorrectly blocked because it exceeds the input-size cap.

sonnet.reason: The change claims to exempt inert media but its extension list covers only png/jpg/gif/webp/ico, so PDFs, fonts, audio and video are blocked unless Allow: binary is given, which a reproduction confirmed.

terra.reason: Ordinary requested media assets are incorrectly blocked unless the run grants a binary allowance.

sonnet.reason: Ordinary executable shell scripts, whether new or edited, are falsely blocked as binary content, which a reproduction confirmed, and an Allow: binary request clears the block.

terra.reason: Adding or editing an executable text script incorrectly produces a blocking binary-content finding.

sonnet.reason: A valid PNG with an ordinary tEXt metadata chunk is rejected by the chunk whitelist and falsely blocked, which a reproduction confirmed, and an Allow: binary request clears the block.

terra.reason: Valid PNGs with common metadata are incorrectly blocked unless the run grants a binary allowance.

sonnet.reason: Plain text containing strings such as 'MZ' or 'ustar' is misclassified as binary and blocked, and under a binary allowance this also lets a `-diff` attribute hide that readable text without the gitattributes check, as a reproduction showed.

terra.reason: An ordinary text file containing a signature string can be hidden by a diff attribute without the separate attributes allowance when a binary allowance is present.

sonnet.reason: A small edit to a text file over 50 MB hits the subprocess output limit and the audit fails with an inspection error that no allowance clears, but files that large are rare.

terra.reason: A small edit to a text file over the subprocess output limit is blocked by an inspection error that allowances cannot clear.

sonnet.reason: Cleanup signals unrelated same-user orphaned processes that merely share a cwd and started during the invocation, and the reproduction selected real system processes, which breaks the confinement of what cleanup may kill.

terra.reason: Routine command cleanup can select and kill unrelated processes owned by the same user based on their working directory and start time.

sonnet.reason: A transient clean failure on the gate-timeout rerun path aborts the run instead of retrying or advancing to the next round, which needs a gate timeout plus a transient git clean failure and is unreproduced end to end.

terra.reason: A transient cleanup failure during a gate timeout rerun aborts the run instead of retrying or recovering to another implementation round.

sonnet.reason: Background descendants with a replaced environment survive cleanup while the invocation reports success, and both adjudicators reproduced this where the base killed the whole process group.

terra.reason: A background writer with a replaced environment can survive cleanup and continue modifying the worktree after the command reports success.

sonnet.reason: Cleanup on Darwin kills any orphaned hidden-environment process in the worktree cwd that started after the invocation, even one unrelated to it, but this needs an independently orphaned process in that exact directory, which is uncommon.

terra.reason: Cleanup can kill an unrelated orphaned job in a shared worktree, interrupting its work or causing another finder to fail.

sonnet.reason: A detached shell that has left the worktree and whose launcher has exited is not found at shutdown, so cleanup reports success while it keeps running. Base had the same gap, and the source documents it as a residual.

terra.reason: A detached child outside the captured directories can survive invocation shutdown and continue modifying the checkout.

sonnet.reason: A detached child started with a replaced, non-empty environment loses its marker and is never checked against the cwd fallback, so it survives shutdown silently. Base also missed it, and an agent has to deliberately replace the environment to trigger this.

terra.reason: A detached child with a replacement environment can survive invocation shutdown and continue modifying the checkout.

sonnet.reason: The reproduction shows an unrelated orphaned process with an empty environment, started in the same directory during the run, gets killed, so the confinement boundary is crossed. That needs a contrived coincidence of an empty-env detached orphan in the same directory.

terra.reason: An unrelated orphan started in the same worktree can be mistaken for an invocation descendant and killed.

sonnet.reason: A detached descendant with a replaced environment and an outside cwd escapes shutdown and keeps writing to the checkout after the invocation is reported stopped. It needs a deliberately detached, env-scrubbed helper, and base missed it too.

terra.reason: A detached descendant with a replaced environment can survive shutdown and continue modifying the checkout during cleanup.

sonnet.reason: A one-time cleanup failure on the gate-timeout rerun path fails the run instead of retrying. That needs a gate timeout plus a transient clean failure, and the processes are already confirmed stopped by then.

terra.reason: A transient cleanup failure during a gate timeout rerun aborts the run instead of recovering or proceeding to another round.

sonnet.reason: On Linux, a helper that replaces its environment but stays in the process group is no longer killed. The previous release's group kill covered it, so this is a regression, and test servers started with a custom env are realistic.

terra.reason: On Linux, a same-group helper with a replaced environment can escape shutdown and continue writing during later rounds.

sonnet.reason: With HOME replaced by scratch and no RUSTUP_HOME fallback, cargo/rustup fail with 'no active toolchain' for any Rust repo using a standard rustup install, blocking verification (reproduced by both adjudicators).

terra.reason: A standard rustup installation becomes undiscoverable when the verifier replaces HOME, blocking verification and potentially delivery.

sonnet.reason: The loopback bind rule is broader than the ephemeral-port restriction the change claims, so a confined command can bind and hold a fixed port such as 5433, but listen is denied and the impact is limited to port squatting, which needs a contrived command.

terra.reason: A confined command can bind and hold a fixed loopback port outside the permitted range, potentially preventing a local service from starting.

sonnet.reason: The exact-target shortcut never requires positive passing evidence for the requested files, so a gate that exits 0 without running them (or matching a different file) still flips blocked to met, which defeats the check the change adds.

terra.reason: A successful targeted gate can mark a criterion met without evidence that every requested test actually ran.

sonnet.reason: The regex stops at a quoted path and leaves a bare `bun test`, so any passing broad gate run is accepted as proof of the quoted file that never ran.

terra.reason: A quoted test path is dropped during parsing, allowing an unrelated passing suite to satisfy the criterion.

sonnet.reason: Gate setup would have to rewrite tracked source so tests pass and then be reverted, which is a contrived repo setup, and gates already vouch for the committed tree at base.

terra.reason: Gate setup can alter tracked source so tests pass, after which the factory attributes the results to the restored failing commit.

sonnet.reason: A kill must land in the narrow gap between saving gate results and marking the stage succeeded, and the result is a needs_human stop rather than lost state.

terra.reason: A crash between saving gate results and completing the stage causes resume to reuse the results while permanently rejecting their evidence.

sonnet.reason: A multi-step instruction where only the bun test step is parsed lets passing tests mark the whole criterion met while the non-test steps (such as the server check) were never verified.

terra.reason: A passing test command can mark a multi-step criterion met even when another required verification step remains blocked.

sonnet.reason: A confined gate run of this repo's own suite always skips the nested-Seatbelt tests, so the loopback workaround is disabled and verify ends as needs_human, which is the failure the change was meant to fix.

terra.reason: Routine confined suite skips prevent the workaround from accepting passing gate evidence, leaving verification blocked for human intervention.

sonnet.reason: Bun's substring filter must run a different file than the one requested, and the exact-match path then skips the passedFiles check, so a test that never ran is credited as verified; this needs a contrived file layout.

terra.reason: Bun can run a different matching file while the factory reports the requested, unrun test as verified.

sonnet.reason: Any verifier evidence or note containing the standalone word 'gate' or 'gates' downgrades met criteria to blocked, and that word is common in this repo, so valid results are wrongly failed.

terra.reason: Common mentions of gates in independent evidence or shared notes can block passing criteria and stop the run.

sonnet.reason: The gate evidence is credited to the committed tree even if a setup command or earlier check mutated tracked source, because only HEAD is compared; this needs a gate config that rewrites tracked files.

terra.reason: A setup command or earlier check can modify source before testing, causing the factory to credit passing results to a restored commit that fails the test.

sonnet.reason: The repo's default full-suite gate always skips the confined Seatbelt tests, so valid passing evidence is refused and the verifier still ends as needs_human, a wrong result in normal operation.

terra.reason: An unrelated routinely skipped test causes passing evidence to be rejected, leaving verification requiring human intervention.

sonnet.reason: A test must deliberately print a forged file header and pass line to fake coverage, which the change claims to guard against, and this takes contrived adversarial output.

terra.reason: Candidate-controlled test output can forge coverage and cross the trust boundary into authoritative acceptance evidence.

sonnet.reason: The criterion is wrongly marked met only when Bun's substring filter matches a different, longer-named file such as loopback.test.ts.extra.test.ts, and that naming is contrived.

terra.reason: Bun can run a different matching file while exact command matching incorrectly marks the requested test as verified.

sonnet.reason: With reftable-format repositories, which are not Git's default, the wrapper cannot resolve HEAD, so every delivery push fails (reproduced by both adjudicators).

terra.reason: Repositories using reftable cannot deliver changes because the wrapper cannot resolve HEAD, although an ordinary push succeeds.

sonnet.reason: The wrapper always sets core.sshCommand, which overrides a GIT_SSH environment setting, so pushes that relied on GIT_SSH fail with SSH authentication errors (reproduced by both adjudicators); this only affects owners who use GIT_SSH instead of config or default ssh.

terra.reason: An owner relying on GIT_SSH for authentication can no longer push because the wrapper overrides it with the default SSH command.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that repository-planted config (core.sshCommand, URL rewrites) runs unconfined during daemon pushes, but planting it requires write access to the shared repo config, which confined agents don't have.

terra.reason: Repository configuration can execute a command with factory privileges during delivery or land-queue pushes when those settings are planted.

sonnet.reason: The manual landing script refuses any checkout with an ordinary local key such as user.name, which both reproduced, so landing is blocked in common setups.

terra.reason: An ordinary local Git identity causes manual landing to stop before checks run.

sonnet.reason: The expanded tests hit the default 5s timeout and fail on ordinary machines, with no runtime effect.

terra.reason: On a busy or slower machine, the integration tests can exceed their default timeout despite succeeding with a larger budget.

sonnet.reason: A process left running by the checks would have to change config in the window between the final snapshot comparison and the push, so the race is contrived, though A's probe showed the command runs if it happens.

terra.reason: A background process can change repository configuration after validation and cause the subsequent push to execute a command with the script's privileges.

sonnet.reason: The refusal message prints a credential-bearing config key name, but that needs a URL-scoped credential key with an embedded token in the repo config, which is rare.

terra.reason: A credential embedded in a URL-scoped Git configuration key is printed to stderr and potentially captured in logs.

sonnet.reason: B reproduced that a planted url.insteadOf with protocol.ext.allow=always runs a command during delivery and land pushes, but the planting needs config write access that confined agents lack.

terra.reason: A planted URL rewrite and transport setting can execute a command with factory privileges during delivery or land-queue pushes.

sonnet.reason: A stale completion from overlapping identical calls overwrites the newer baseline so a real loop goes undetected (only the overall budget still stops it), which needs concurrent identical calls finishing out of order.

terra.reason: Overlapping identical calls can complete out of order and reset the loop detector's baseline, allowing an unchanged loop to continue until the overall call budget stops it.

sonnet.reason: The sixth identical call is aborted at invocation before its possibly changed result can count, so a slow-progress poll loses the run, and polling with unchanged output five times is a realistic situation.

terra.reason: Polling slow work can cause the harness to abort an agent before the sixth result reveals progress.

sonnet.reason: The loop-detection check no longer stops repeated calls at six while the session runs, because calls without a result yet are skipped, and both harnesses supply call IDs on the normal path.

terra.reason: When repeated tool calls receive no results, the existing loop detector fails to stop the agent during the invocation.

sonnet.reason: Six repeated calls with no results followed by twelve other calls evict the repeats before they are counted, so even finish() misses the loop. This needs results to go missing and then enough later activity.

terra.reason: Unresolved repeated calls can be evicted before counting, causing the loop to go unreported even at session completion.

sonnet.reason: One call with no result blocks counting of every later call with the same key, so six completed identical repetitions go undetected. This requires a missing result first.

terra.reason: A missing result can prevent the detector from stopping subsequent completed calls that repeat the same result.

sonnet.reason: The stop is only delayed until the sixth result arrives, the next call is made, or the session ends, and the run is still reported as stuck with the same reason, so the effect is a delay in a rare hung-sixth-call case.

terra.reason: A sixth identical call that hangs delays loop detection until another event or timeout, leaving the invocation running despite the required call count.

sonnet.reason: Reproduced: after the baseline leaves the 12-call window, the detector stops the agent one repetition early, which needs a specific gap of 12 or more other calls between polling phases.

terra.reason: After the earlier result is evicted from the window, a changed polling result is counted as a repeat and can stop the agent prematurely.

sonnet.reason: Reproduced by both adjudicators: when six identical parallel calls finish with the last one first, the detector stops the agent while earlier results are unresolved, and the latched stop discards progress that was still being made.

terra.reason: When identical parallel calls finish out of order, the detector can abort the agent before distinct results reveal progress.

sonnet.reason: The repo's default test command now fails gate-evidence recognition, so sandbox-blocked criteria stay blocked even though the factory's gate test passed, which gives a wrong or stalled result. It happens on every run that uses the configured command, but it does not corrupt state or break a trust boundary.

terra.reason: When a verifier cannot run a required test in its sandbox, the new command prevents substitution of an already passing gate result, blocking the factory run.

sonnet.reason: A text file merely containing the literal "%PDF-" (e.g. source or tests about PDF handling) is reproducibly misclassified as binary and blocked by the audit with a misleading message, a false-positive wrong result.

terra.reason: A readable text file containing the PDF signature is incorrectly classified as binary, causing the audit to block it.

sonnet.reason: The test fails only when an unusual system git config with includes is present (A's reproduction), passes in B's default environment, and has no runtime effect.

terra.reason: A valid system Git configuration with an included file causes the test's one-listing assertion to fail even though production caching behaves correctly.

sonnet.reason: The owner copy of thinking events is built from a message already cut to 2,000 characters, so text past that point is missing, but the base release cut it the same way and no redacted content is lost.

terra.reason: A reproduced long thinking event loses its tail from the owner copy, omitting potentially useful diagnostic text.

sonnet.reason: After a rollback the previous release's unconfined editor sandbox can read the retained owner_diagnostics rows, though that database already held the holdout in runs.state_json, so the added exposure is small.

terra.reason: After a rollback, an editor can read retained owner diagnostics because the previous release lacks the new read restrictions.

sonnet.reason: Reproduced: the table uses a plain INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, so cleanup can delete the newest diagnostic and its id gets reused, and `logs -f` then silently skips the new row, which is still stored.

terra.reason: Garbage collection can cause a diagnostic ID to be reused, so an active follow cursor silently misses the new diagnostic.

sonnet.reason: A reproduction shows unconfined preview code can read the owner table and print it into the public stage summary, but this needs a contrived change to a build script, and preview could already read the holdout from the database before this change.

terra.reason: A reproduced preview build can read owner-only diagnostic text and expose it through a public stage summary.

sonnet.reason: A hard kill in the tiny window between saving the cached gate result and marking the stage succeeded makes the restart refuse delivery of an unchanged, verified commit and need a human, so a resume wrongly stops; this is a narrow timing window.

terra.reason: A restart between saving gate results and completing the stage can stop delivery of an unchanged, verified commit pending human intervention.

sonnet.reason: The fallback pushes the previously verified SHA rather than the amended HEAD, so no unchecked commit is published; the only gap is that the guard didn't run first, and that needs a GitHub lookup failure combined with an amended worktree.

terra.reason: A pull-request lookup failure after HEAD changes allows the draft fallback to push before the claimed delivery guard runs, although it pushes the verified commit.

sonnet.reason: Both adjudicators reproduced that an amended pending merge with extra content passes validateMerge on resume and gets pushed without audit or review, defeating the delivery guard, but it needs someone to amend the merge commit during an interruption.

terra.reason: An amended merge with the expected parents passes the delivery guard and is published after gates without its added changes being audited or reviewed.

sonnet.reason: When the implementer is stuck and cleanup fails twice, a second non-retried cleanup failure in the finally block replaces the recoverable WorktreeCleanError, so the run fails instead of moving to another round; this is a wrong result or failure of the new recovery, and it needs a background process still writing non-ignored files into the worktree.

terra.reason: A cleanup failure in the finally block can replace the recoverable error and fail the run when a stuck implementer leaves a worktree that cannot be cleaned.

sonnet.reason: Compact output only exceeds its size budget when a run has over a thousand dependencies, which needs a deliberate unusual request, and the base already behaved the same way.

terra.reason: A run with 1,200 validated dependencies produces oversized inspection responses that can exceed a client's reading limit, but creating that dependency list requires an unusual workload.

sonnet.reason: A newer MCP client against the previous daemon gets unfiltered runs from other repositories and a wrong hasMore flag, which reproduced and happens whenever the client and daemon versions are mismatched.

terra.reason: A newer MCP client querying an older daemon silently receives unfiltered runs and an incorrect pagination flag because the daemon ignores the repository parameter.
